_source.description: Battle.net product table, launch/install/uninstall rules and product.db protobuf schema, transcribed from Playnite's BattleNetLibrary extension.
_source.repo: https://codeberg.org/CrowIsTaken/PlayniteExtensions (branch main10, commit f008798eb06c6eb1e9cc48711a5a56d470c2cf2d, 2026-10-18); byte-identical to the archived GitHub copy https://github.com/JosefNemec/PlayniteExtensions (master, commit 886468f65724e6fd104f3a09847a17ba57cfb430) for every BattleNetLibrary .cs file
_source.license: MIT, Copyright (c) 2020 Josef Nemec (LICENSE.md of both repos). Keep this notice when reusing the table.
_source.note_on_duplicates: The C# table contains the W1R and W2R entries twice (BattleNetGames.cs lines 343-374 repeat lines 323-358). Only one copy is kept here; FirstOrDefault semantics make the duplicate harmless in Playnite.

installation_path.method: Enumerate the Windows Uninstall registry (HKLM and HKCU, both Registry64 and Registry32 views: SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*) and take the entry whose UninstallString contains the substring "-uid=battle.net"; InstallLocation of that entry is the client directory.

client.running_detection: Process.GetProcessesByName("Battle.net").Count > 0 (BattleNet.cs:28-29); when the client has to be started before a launch, Playnite waits until at least 5 'Battle.net' processes exist, then an extra 5 s (BattleNetGameController.cs:206-211)

product_db.format: Protocol Buffers (binary). Playnite deserializes the WHOLE file as protobuf-net `InstalledProductInfo[]`, i.e. it reads only root field 1 (repeated ProductInstall) and ignores every other root field.

InstallData.1: string Path  (= install_path, e.g. "C:/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft"; Playnite runs Paths.FixSeparators on it)

full_schema_second_source.source: product_db.proto in https://github.com/FriendsOfGalaxy/galaxy-integration-battlenet/tree/master/src (consistent with Playnite's field numbers; fields beyond what Playnite reads are UNVERIFIED against Blizzard's own definition)

how_playnite_uses_it: product.db is a FALLBACK: the registry Uninstall entries are scanned first (see registry_detection); product.db entries are added only for ProductIds not already found (BattleNetLibrary.cs:139-179).

Each product_install is matched to the static table by case-insensitive EXACT equality of uid == InternalId, restricted to Type == Default (BattleNetLibrary.cs:155-156). Entries with no match (e.g. uid 'battle.net', 'agent', 'bna') are skipped.

GameId := ProductId from the table, Name := table Name, InstallDirectory := Paths.FixSeparators(install_path), IsInstalled := true. (Playnite does NOT check base_product_state.installed/playable nor that the directory exists for product.db entries.)

steps: Enumerate Uninstall entries (HKLM+HKCU, 64-bit and 32-bit views). Skip entries with empty UninstallString or empty InstallLocation.

Regex on UninstallString: Battle\.net.*--uid=(.*?)\s  (NOTE: Battle.net game uninstall strings look like "C:\ProgramData\Battle.net\Agent\Blizzard Uninstaller.exe" --lang=enUS --uid=wow_enus --displayname="World of Warcraft"; group 1 is the uid, e.g. wow_enus).
Skip if DisplayName ends with "Test" or "Beta".
Match captured uid against the table with: product = Games.FirstOrDefault(a => a.Type == Default && uid.StartsWith(a.InternalId, OrdinalIgnoreCase)) (prefix match, so wow_enus -> wow -> WoW).
Skip if InstallLocation directory does not exist.

Game: GameId = ProductId, Name = table Name (RemoveTrademarks), InstallDirectory = InstallLocation, Source = "Battle.net", Platforms = [pc_windows]. First occurrence wins when several versions are installed.

Classic games (no uid): entry.Publisher == "Blizzard Entertainment" AND entry.DisplayName equals a Classic product's InternalId ("Diablo II" or "Warcraft III"); then for every Classic product with that InternalId, the game is installed only if <InstallLocation>\<ClassicExecutable> exists (so D2 and D2X both map to the 'Diablo II' entry; D2X exists only if Diablo II.exe exists -- both use the same exe in the table).
registry_detection.uninstall_entry_for_a_product: GetUninstallEntry(app): Classic -> entry.DisplayName == app.InternalId; Default -> Regex(UninstallString, "Battle\.net.*--uid=<InternalId>.*\s", IgnoreCase) (BattleNetLibrary.cs:34-61)

play_default.command: "<client InstallLocation>\Battle.net.exe" --exec="launch <ProductId>"   e.g. --exec="launch WoW", --exec="launch Pro"  (BattleNetGameController.cs:216; Game.GameId is the ProductId)
play_default.precondition: If no 'Battle.net' process is running: start Battle.net.exe, poll every 1 s until >= 5 'Battle.net' processes exist, wait 5 s more, then send --exec (BattleNetGameController.cs:200-212).
play_default.tracking: ProcessMonitor.WatchDirectoryProcesses(Game.InstallDirectory, alreadyRunning:false) -> polls Process.GetProcesses() every 2 s; TreeStarted fires when a process whose main-module path contains the (junction-resolved) install dir appears, TreeDestroyed when none is left; session length = Stopwatch between the two.

play_classic.tracking: TreeStarted invoked immediately; ProcessMonitor.WatchDirectoryProcesses(dir, alreadyRunning:true, byProcessNames:true) -> matches running processes by executable FILE NAME found under the install dir (BattleNetGameController.cs:188-191)

actions.install_default: "<client>\Battle.net.exe" --game=<InternalId>   (BattleNetGameController.cs:54); then poll GetUninstallEntry(app) every 10 s until present (install dir = entry.InstallLocation)
actions.install_classic: Opens https://battle.net/support/article/256212 for W3C/W3CX, https://battle.net/support/article/13867 otherwise (BattleNetGameController.cs:38-45)
actions.uninstall: cmd /C "<entry.UninstallString>" where entry = GetUninstallEntry(product); poll every 2 s until the entry disappears (BattleNetGameController.cs:108-145)
actions.play_time: No local source. Playnite's online account import (BattleNetAccountClient, login required) only provides ownership (titleId -> ApiId); Playtime/LastActivity for Battle.net games come solely from Playnite's own session tracking.

field_semantics.ProductId: Battle.net product code (case-insensitive compare). Used as Playnite GameId and as the argument of --exec="launch <ProductId>".
field_semantics.InternalId: Battle.net uid prefix as it appears in Uninstall UninstallString --uid=<uid> (e.g. wow_enus) and as product.db ProductInstall.uid. For Classic games it is the Uninstall DisplayName instead. Used as the argument of --game=<InternalId> for installs.
field_semantics.ApiId: titleId returned by the Battle.net account API (https://account.battle.net/api/games-and-subs); only needed for the (out of scope) account import.
field_semantics.Type: Default = launched through the Battle.net client; Classic = legacy standalone installers launched directly via ClassicExecutable.
field_semantics.IconUrl/BackgroundUrl/CoverUrl: Remote artwork URLs used by BattleNetMetadataProvider (no local artwork is read from disk by this plugin).
